headline: Northwind Pay is at a critical juncture: EU banking licence now in hand, regulator expects unified audit-grade SIEM, and their Datadog spend (4M annually plus unpredictable overages) is the economic driver for consolidation by Q3 2026.

sections.heading: Strategic Context & Opportunity
bullets: Northwind Pay secured EU banking licence Q3 2025 after 3-year wait, unlocking deposit-taking and lending; regulator now mandates unified SIEM and audit-ready observability across all systems.
Current stack fragmentation (Datadog for metrics, Splunk for SIEM, Grafana+Prometheus for infra, Elasticsearch on some workloads) creates three separate on-call rotations and compliance blind spots.

Datadog renewal November 1, 2026 at ~4M annually; Finance is forecasting 12-month renewal vs consolidation scenarios. Peak ingest spike during card promos last cycle cost 80k in overages, fueling cost predictability pressure.
Sarah Chen (VP Engineering) sponsors, CTO approves, Mike Taylor (Platform Lead) runs technical eval. Decision timeline: end of Q3 2026. Migration window: 6 months before Datadog renewal.

sections.heading: Recent Signals & Regulatory Pressure
bullets: Auditor flagged SIEM coverage gap as part of EU banking licence audit prep (P1 open ticket); this is a compliance blocker, not a nice-to-have.
50M+ retail customers across 38 countries on multi-cloud (AWS, GCP); heavy Kafka + Kubernetes footprint means native K8s ingestion and event streaming integration are non-negotiable.
Secondary share sale completed; investor and board now scrutinizing OpEx. Consolidation conversation is linked to investor confidence in margin expansion and operational efficiency.

sections.heading: Technical & Commercial Pain Points
bullets: Ingest at scale is the hard constraint: Mike Taylor stated POC must succeed at 80k events per second (peak campaign load). Failure to hit that target kills Elastic evaluation entirely.

7-year audit retention at Frankfurt + Dublin regions requires predictable, tiered storage costs (hot 7 days, warm 30, cold searchable snapshots). Datadog has no equivalent cost control mechanism at that scale.
SIEM must map to MITRE ATT&CK framework and pass regulator expectations for EU financial services (PSD2, AML/KYC audit trails). Splunk integration today is point-in-time, not unified.

sections.heading: Discovery & Validation Questions
bullets: Confirm the 80k EPS baseline is sustained for how long during peak (hours, days?) and whether that includes trace ingest or is logs+metrics only.
Walk Mike through Elastic cross-cluster search (CCS/CCR) topology for break-glass investigations; clarify whether regulator expects real-time query sync or eventual consistency is acceptable.

Understand Splunk contract end date and any professional services lock-in (e.g., custom dashboards, tuning); Elastic AutoOps eliminates the need for expensive cluster health diagnostics (Splunk PS engagement typically 15k-25k per review).
Ask Sarah about procurement process and timeline for vendor discussions; she flagged two-week slip last cycle. Loop in procurement contact early to unblock approval workflows.

sections.heading: Talking Points & Value Mapping
bullets: Cost consolidation: Replace Datadog (4M) + Splunk (est. 1.5M including PS) + Prometheus/Grafana maintenance with unified Elastic Cloud. Model shows 35-45% TCO reduction year-one, driven by index tiering and searchable snapshots at 7-year retention.

Splunk to Elastic SIEM transition: Elastic Security + Detection Engine covers MITRE ATT&CK natively; AutoOps is free on all tiers and surfaces root-cause cluster health without requiring Professional Services engagements (unlike Splunk cluster health reviews at 15k-25k per engagement). Immediate saving relative to Splunk's diagnostic model.

Kafka integration: Elastic connectors for Kafka ingest at 80k EPS with native backpressure handling. Reference architecture: Frankfurt + Dublin hot (i3), warm (d3), cold (searchable snapshots on GCS) for EU compliance.

Single pane for logs, metrics, traces, SIEM: Reduces on-call cognitive load, simplifies audit evidence chain for PSD2/AML. Regulatory mapping document will detail how Elastic Security satisfies EU banking expectations.

sections.heading: Risks & Open Questions
bullets: POC execution risk: 80k EPS POC must complete before end of Q2 2026 to allow 6-month migration before November 1 Datadog renewal. Any delay compresses decision window. Propose POC start-date in current week.
Splunk SIEM rules migration: Unclear how much custom logic exists in Splunk today; if rules are complex, migration effort may exceed 4-week sprint. Request Splunk SIEM ruleset audit early.
Procurement sign-off: Sarah mentioned prior 2-week slip. Confirm procurement contact and alignment with vendor evaluation RFI before next meeting.
GCP searchable snapshots availability in Frankfurt region: Confirm GCS integration for cold-tier snapshots; if unavailable, fall back to S3 and model cross-region transfer costs.

sections.heading: Next Steps & Meeting Prep
bullets: Send POC plan covering 80k EPS ingest, SIEM MITRE ATT&CK coverage, and Datadog vs Elastic cost model (target: Tuesday post-meeting).
Draft regulatory mapping document for EU banking expectations (PSD2, AML audit trails, retention, cross-cluster search break-glass).
Request Splunk SIEM ruleset snapshot and Datadog contract renewal terms from Sarah's team before follow-up Tuesday meeting.
Confirm reference architecture (Frankfurt hot/warm, Dublin hot/warm, GCS cold tier, CCS/CCR topology) with Mike's platform team by Friday.

sections.heading: Attendee Context
bullets: Rodrigo Careaga (Elastic FE): Has already scoped two prior deep-dive calls with Mike on topology and ILM; owns POC delivery and regulatory mapping.
Sarah Chen (VP Engineering): Executive sponsor, decision-maker, procurement gatekeeper. Motivated by cost and compliance. Prefers structured timelines and early vendor alignment.
Mike Taylor (Platform Lead): Technical evaluator, Kubernetes + Kafka expert, owns POC execution success criteria. Skeptical; 80k EPS is the gating test.
